subject: Mutual Action Plan touchpoint — data handling & deployment mode decisions (VPC vs on‑prem)
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@solacehealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Victor Huang <victor.huang@solacehealth.com>, Solace Procurement <procurement@solacehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP check-in: deployment & retention decisions before legal review

Thanks Priyom/Jordan — quick touch before we hand the MAP to Legal next week. A few targeted questions we need firm decisions on so Legal can scope contract language: 

1) Deployment mode: can Redwood commit to a VPC-hosted instance in our AWS account, or will on‑prem be required for certain data classes? We need to mark this as "VPC preferred" vs "on‑prem required" per the table in the draft MAP.

2) Retention: for PHI-adjacent logs (diagnostic metadata only) — are we able to enforce a 30‑day rolling retention with secure-delete hooks? If not, what is the minimum retention we can commit to?

3) PII handling: Solace will send hashed identifiers plus raw contact info for outreach. We need confirmation on separation of data paths and whether contact info can be tokenized before it hits the model host.

Please reply with explicit choices so I can update the MAP. Attached: our current MAP worksheet and the evidence checklist Legal asked for.

—Elena
Director, Product Integrations
Solace Health

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MAP check-in: deployment & retention decisions before legal review

Elena — thanks for the clear ask. Summary of our position after the internal sync below (short answers first):

- Deployment mode: VPC-in-customer-account is supported for this engagement (Redwood Private VPC mode). On‑prem (air‑gapped) is possible but requires an addendum and a 6–8 week ops lead time. Mark: "VPC in AWS account — preferred and supported".

- Retention: we can commit to a configurable retention policy down to 30 days for diagnostic logs with secure deletion hooks (we log minimal request metadata by default). For full request traces (session-level debug captures) retention requires explicit opt-in and will default to 90 days unless turned off.

- PII handling: we recommend tokenization at the customer edge (Solace) before sending contact info. If Solace cannot tokenize, Redwood can offer an ingestion layer that hashes / tokenizes PII prior to model routing, but this adds a small latency and an ops onboarding task.

Actionable next items (owners below). I'll also attach a short comparison doc for your legal team.

Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: MAP check-in: deployment & retention decisions before legal review

Hi all — adding a few compliance/operational clarifications from our security checklist: 

- Data classification: If Solace classifies contact info as PII but not PHI, tokenization is acceptable. If contact info is PHI (e.g., includes clinical notes), we require a dedicated SCC and SOC2 evidence matrix to proceed on VPC. I've attached our SOC2 evidence listing for quick reference.

- Key management: For VPC-in-customer-account, we recommend KMS integration with customer-managed keys (CMKs). Redwood supports both CMKs and our managed keys; please indicate preference.

- Audit & logging: We can emit audit logs to an S3 bucket in the customer account with a lifecycle rule matching the retention window. Secure-delete hooks will issue object deletion and confirm by checksum. The 30‑day rolling retention for diagnostic metadata is feasible if Solace agrees to the lifecycle policy we propose.

I'll add these notes into the MAP worksheet. 

Neha
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks team — captured and consolidated. Below is the MAP update and explicit action items for Solace handoff to Legal (so Elena can paste into the MAP column):

MAP decisions (to insert into the "Deployment & Data" column):
- Deployment: Redwood to provision in-customer-account VPC (Redwood Private VPC mode). On‑prem remains an optional addendum (6–8 week ops lead time; additional deployment fee).
- Retention: Diagnostic metadata retention configurable to 30 days (secure-delete lifecycle enforced). Full request tracing requires explicit opt-in and defaults to 90 days.
- PII: Tokenization at customer edge preferred. Redwood can provide an ingestion tokenization layer if required (minor latency and additional onboarding task).
- KMS: Recommended customer-managed KMS (CMK) for key custody; Redwood-managed keys available as fallback.
- Audit: Audit logs exported to customer S3 bucket; lifecycle rules enforce retention window; secure-delete webhook/confirmation provided.

Action items (owner — due date):
1) Elena / Solace Product: Confirm whether contact info will be tokenized at the edge or if Redwood should provide tokenization. (Owner: Elena Torres) — Due: 2027-06-18
2) Priyom: Prepare short ingestion tokenization spec and ops checklist for Solace if they choose Redwood tokenization. (Owner: Priyom Das) — Due: 2027-06-17
3) Neha: Generate the SOC2 evidence snapshot and KMS integration checklist for Legal to review. (Owner: Neha Kapoor) — Due: 2027-06-16
4) Jordan / Finance: Prepare a line-item estimate for Dedicated/Private VPC reserved capacity and on‑prem deployment fee to include in the MAP. (Owner: Jordan Blake) — Due: 2027-06-18
5) Elena / Procurement: Share preferred CMK ARN or indicate Redwood-managed keys. (Owner: Solace Procurement) — Due: 2027-06-18

Please reply only to acknowledge if these look correct; we will update the MAP master and hand to Legal after confirmations above.

—Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
